hypothesis: For the 6mm wheel-first ridge, delaying brake onset may avoid braking during the early caster crossing while retaining authority before driven-wheel contact.

only_candidate_change.reason: Round up the observed caster-end minus trigger interval (~0.148s) to the next 0.1s control interval; this is one experimental value, not a validated clearance detector.

timing_limitation: Using the old 0.077s trigger plus0.2s delay plus clean-floor239–254ms body response leaves only ~76–91ms before the observed0.607s driven contact. Contact timing is trajectory-dependent; this arithmetic is not a guarantee.
implementation_prerequisites: New explicit research contract; preserve existing default governor and study scores
Zero-delay output reproduces the current controller
Pending delay lasts exactly two control intervals; first ramp step at trigger+0.2s
Same ramp/bounds/hold/recovery behavior once braking starts
Stop, stale feedback and fault cancel pending delay without stale/full-speed command replay
Log trigger stamp, brake-onset stamp, executed commands and phase timers separately
fixed: Robot, solid floor, PI, detector, observations, speed bounds, target0.90, minhold0.8s, maxhold1.0s, ramp0.4/s, native metrics and physical arrival/stop criteria
comparison: Retain all three arms, all failures, full-route and unchanged crossing metrics. Candidate must preserve existing time/tracking limits; do not replace them with an easier gate after seeing results.
stop_rule: One timing candidate only. Stop on missing reporting or physical failure, no retries. Mixed/no quality benefit at the budget limit rejects this delay hypothesis for the tested scope; do not automatically try more delay/ramp/penalty values.
interpretation: This is a development mechanism test, not a generalization or hardware test. Improvements in both new seed blocks would justify separately budgeted confirmation, not automatic H1/predictor/PPO/Optuna release. Retain the22mm mixed results; do not promote by selecting the easier height.
